sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 32520 of 2024
Applicant :- Sandeep Alias Toote

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Indrajeet Kumar Shukla,Kaushal Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard SriKaushal Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Yogesh Mishra, learned State
Law Officer for the State and perused the record.
2. This is this third bail application.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 299 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 304B, 316 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Jhunsi, District Prayagraj, during the pendency of trial.

4. As a new ground, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is languishing in jail since 25.03.2019, as such, about five years and eight months have been passed and only five witnesses have been examined by the prosecution and six witnesses are yet to be examined.

The trial Sandeep Alias Toote vs State Of U.P. on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76522817/
1 is moving at snail's pace and there is no likelihood of early conclusion of the trial in near future.

entities.text: Sandeep Alias Toote vs State Of U.P. on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is cooperating in trial.
Learned counsel has further stated that the Fundamental Rights of the applicant enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stands violated.
5. Per contra, learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail.

6. The instant case does not fall within the category of taking care of the Fundamental Rights of the applicant only because there are Fundamental Rights of the victim also as there is dying declaration of the deceased which is on record and the deceased has specifically nominated the applicant to be the perpetrator of the crime.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the applicant has been nominated in the dying declaration by the deceased person, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
8. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

9. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
